normalized.governing_thought: Raise prices on mid-market and enterprise renewals in 2027; hold SMB prices until a test shows a rise is safe
executive_summary: Raise prices on mid-market and enterprise renewals in 2027; hold SMB prices until a test shows a rise is safe

1 Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort, not from a reaction to list prices – About 90% of the rise in lost customers is promotion customers – Fixing the promotion cohort cuts SMB churn by a third, not by half (p. 5–10)
2 Larger customers should carry a 10% rise, checked against a renewal control group – A 10% rise left mid-market conversion at 23.1% against 23.6% (p. 12–15)

3 SMB is where a rise could backfire: Inkwell sells at $9 against our $15 – Win rate in SMB deals with Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year – A 12% rise stops paying at twice the 2023 churn response (p. 17–21)

4 A segmented rise adds about $4.3M and can reach 15% growth with little new business – The CFO's $10.3M is about $6.3M after timing, caps and churn – Only $0.6M of new ARR is needed; NRR rises to about 114% (p. 23–26)
5 Reprice larger renewals in January, test SMB first, and re-activate the cohort – Decide SMB prices in July against the 2023 response (p. 28–32)

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices on mid-market and enterprise renewals in 2027; hold SMB prices until a test shows a rise is safe. Option B (Segmented): 10% at renewal for mid-market and uncapped enterprise, 7% where enterprise contracts cap rises; SMB list prices held pending a test (+8% on a random half of non-promotion SMB renewals, Jan–Mar), decided in July; re-activate the promotion cohort through onboarding rather than discounts; read larger-customer renewals against a control group; define logo and revenue churn by segment and cohort for the board.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Most ARR on paper, but $10.3M is nearer $6.3M and rests on SMB (4a); the SMB rise stops adding ARR at 1.98x the 2023 churn response.
Recommended: 10% on larger renewals; SMB decided in July on a test (4b). Meets both targets: only $0.6M new-customer ARR needed, NRR about 114%.
Safest for churn, but new customers must add $4.9M of ARR.

normalized.extraction_notes: The divider slides (4, 11, 16, 22, 27) are titled "Churn comes from the promotion cohort" in the extracted text. That looks like the section 1 label being picked up as the title, but I kept it verbatim. Slide 33 is an appendix contents page, so its claims list is empty. On slide 23, the ratings for the four criteria (Reaches 15% growth, Keeps NRR above 100%, Protects SMB retention, Backed by our own tests) were apparently drawn as graphic circles ("full circle = strongest"), so the cells came out empty and those ratings are missing. The only exception is "n/a" for option C under "Backed by our own tests". Slide 14 refers to "Watch Inkwell moving up (5d)", but the deck has no slide 5d. On slide 32, the Owner cell for the SMB test row reads "Decides SMB prices / The one signal that changes the 2027 plan in July" and does not name an owner. Slide 28's timeline arrives as flat text, so I couldn't tell which quarter each item sits in. There were no images to transcribe; chart values come from the extracted chart data.
